required_legend_notes: Grey marks retain operationally forced conditions. Uncertainty uses whole-seed 95% bootstrap intervals where available.

Ρ = τₚ(largest) / τₚ(smallest), from direct measured heading persistence. The full overview includes every designed model/input comparison. Cell colour shows only a finite measured direct persistence ratio, on a logarithmic colour scale centred at one. Bound or unidentified cells receive no fabricated ratio colour. Up/down arrows denote empirical one-sided bounds, a bar a finite empirical interval, and ? an unidentified or unavailable ratio or regime. A dagger denotes a finite point with upper-unbounded bootstrap confidence interval. Hatching denotes an input not designed for that model. Grey retains operationally forced cells. Letters show the largest-cell native raw regime: S single front, M multiple fronts, L low contrast, X mixed. All empirical/CI bounds, native regime fractions, forcing flags and unavailable reasons remain in the panel CSV.

display_audit.scope: Exact root-reviewed measured component and unabridged source CSV

required_legend_notes: Grey marks retain operationally forced conditions. Uncertainty uses whole-seed 95% bootstrap intervals where available.

Open upward/downward triangles retain native empirical lower/upper bounds. CI∞ marks an upper-unbounded bootstrap confidence interval; CI[0,∞) spans the full nonnegative range. Native zero or unidentified [0,∞) values are text at the logarithmic axis foot; no finite positive endpoint is substituted.

Every declared temporal window and sampling cadence is shown. Circles are native finite ratios; right-pointing open triangles are empirical lower bounds, without a substituted ratio point. Horizontal bars retain whole-seed 95% intervals. A dagger denotes an upper-unbounded confidence interval; its finite confidence lower endpoint remains a vertical cap, distinct from the empirical bound. Main, first half, second half and late quarter refer to the declared analysis windows. Sampling ×2/×4/×8 retains the same independent seed histories.
